ref: incremental-verifier agent prompt, Testing Protocol §2 (python3 -m eval.verify_supported)
what: The verifier CLI run as documented fails with ImportError undefined symbol MPIX_Comm_shrink: the MPIX stub LD_PRELOAD lives only in .tt_chip_scope, which eval_test_runner.sh and run_safe_pytest.sh source but a bare python3 -m eval.verify_supported does not
suggest: Prefix the documented command with source .tt_chip_scope (or have eval.verify_supported avoid importing ttnn._ttnn), so the CLI runs in a chip-scoped checkout

ref: incremental-verifier agent prompt, Testing Protocol §3 (precision baseline: 3-4 shapes, gate PCC + relative RMS, got/true ratio)
what: Two binding sources conflict: the verifier prompt mandates 3-4 shapes (small/medium/larger) while the op spec BB-22 (MUST) limits tests to production cases; and relative RMS / got-true ratio are undefined for constant-output ops (all-zero reference), which the prompt does not address
suggest: Say the precision baseline uses the op spec production cases when a BB-22-style rule exists, and give an exact-output fallback (bit/ULP exactness, abs RMS) for constant or exact-copy ops

ref: op prompt BB-21 (every piece of work in its own named zone) vs. profiler device-ns as the perf gate
what: On sub-microsecond kernels each DeviceZoneScopedN marker costs ~18 ns in the zone build, so splitting work into separate zones to satisfy BB-21 measurably regressed the profiled DEVICE KERNEL DURATION the queue gates on, while the plain build improved; nothing warns about this trade
suggest: Note in the zone/BB-21 guidance that zone markers carry ~15-20 ns each on BH and that, for short kernels, shadowed or tiny work should be folded into an existing zone rather than given its own
